newsitem.title: USA: Former NYC official accused in sting.
newsitem.headline: Former NYC official accused in sting.

text.p: A former New York City deputy mayor was arraigned Wednesday for allegedly patronizing a prostitute who was an undercover police officer, authorities said.
Police said Norman Steisel allegedly approached the woman Tuesday evening in an industrial neighborhood in the city's Brooklyn borough and allegedly offered to pay her for sex.
Steisel was deputy mayor under former Mayor David Dinkins and Sanitation Commissioner under former Mayor Ed Koch. More recently, he has worked as a consultant in waste management.
Steisel, who is married and has two stepchildren, was arraigned in Kings County, New York, Criminal Court on a misdemeanor charge.
He did not enter a plea, and the case was adjourned until next month.
"The family hopes that fair-minded people will not leap to conclusions before all the facts are revealed," his attorney Scott Mollen said.
Police said the incident was part of an undercover sting operation in which five other people were also arrested.
